extracted.intended_audience: researchers, panel chairs and research-administration staff who perform or manage peer review of research proposals, manuscripts or programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for people who assess research (proposals, manuscripts, programmes) — how to prepare, what criteria to apply, and how to write reviewer reports and recommendations. Covers reviewer conduct, evaluation dimensions, scoring and report structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and absence of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must disclose and avoid conflicts of interest and recuse themselves when impartial assessment is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any personal, institutional, financial or collaborative relationships with applicants/authors; if a relevant conflict exists, decline or be removed from the assignment. Where partiality is possible but minor, describe it in the report. Examples: recent co-authorship, direct supervisor/subordinate, shared grant, close personal relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat submitted proposals, manuscripts and review materials as confidential and do not share them outside the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not circulate proposals or use privileged information for personal advantage; anonymise any quotes if sharing with colleagues only for legitimate review reasons. Confidential remarks intended only for the panel should be marked as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise and competence to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept only reviews for which you have sufficient subject-matter expertise and methodological understanding to make a fair judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outside your competence, decline or limit comments to clearly identifiable areas. State the limits of your expertise in the report (e.g. 'I am not an expert in X; my comments focus on Y').

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete reviews within agreed deadlines and notify organisers promptly of delays or inability to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late reviews bias panels and delay funding/publication decisions. If extra time is unavoidable, seek extension early and provide an updated timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and evidence-based assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Base evaluations on evidence in the submission, documented outputs, and verifiable facts rather than unsubstantiated opinion or hearsay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support judgments with examples (e.g. cite specific methodological flaws, missing controls, or missing citations). Avoid ad hominem or value-laden language; explain how evidence leads to your conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of originality and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the work advances knowledge beyond the current state of the art and clearly differentiates from existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate what is new (idea, method, dataset, application) and how it compares to key prior work. Distinguish genuinely novel contributions from incremental or confirmatory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific importance and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the significance of the research question and the likely contribution to the field or societal challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider theoretical, methodological, practical and policy impacts as appropriate. Explain why the proposed outcomes matter and to whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigour and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the methods are suitable, sufficiently detailed, and robust to answer the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing controls, sample size/power issues, statistical weaknesses, unclear procedures, and alternative approaches. Recommend specific methodological improvements where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility, workplan and deliverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed timeline, tasks, milestones and resource allocation make the project likely to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether personnel, facilities and budget match objectives. Flag overly ambitious scope or missing key expertise and suggest realistic adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/Team track record and capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the capability of the PI and team to deliver the project, based on publications, prior grants, technical skills and management experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant strengths and weaknesses in expertise, prior outputs, and evidence of successful project delivery. Consider complementarity of team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical, legal and societal considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the submission addresses required ethical approvals, data protection, animal/human subject safeguards, and broader societal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note absent or insufficient ethics statements, plans for consent/data anonymisation, dual-use risks, or regulatory compliance. Recommend ethical review where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management, transparency and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plans for data sharing, metadata, code availability and methods transparency to enable reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear data-management plans, open-access repositories where appropriate, and sufficient methodological detail for replication. Flag proprietary blockers and suggest mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of resources and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the requested budget and resources are necessary, justified and proportionate to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unjustified or missing budget lines (e.g. equipment, personnel). Suggest reductions or reallocations and flag unrealistic cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, structure and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the submission is clearly written, logically organised and communicates aims, methods and expected outcomes effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to specific unclear sections, inconsistent terminology, missing figures/tables or poorly described methods. Recommend rewording or reorganisation where it would materially affect assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate literature and contextualisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether relevant prior work has been cited and the project is well-situated within existing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note omitted key literature or overreliance on outdated or irrelevant references. Suggest seminal or recent works that should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify major scientific, technical or managerial risks and evaluate the adequacy of proposed mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate the seriousness of each risk and recommend contingency plans or alternative approaches to reduce likelihood/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of ambition versus realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposal strikes an appropriate balance between innovative ambition and realistic deliverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag projects that are too conservative (low innovation) or overly speculative (low chance of success) and recommend recalibration of objectives or phased approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact, dissemination and exploitation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess plans for dissemination, stakeholder engagement, knowledge transfer and potential socioeconomic impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete dissemination activities, target audiences, exploitation/commercialisation routes, and realistic metrics for impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, specific report structure (summary, major/minor issues, recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports should start with a concise summary, list major strengths and weaknesses, provide actionable suggestions and end with a clear overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short non-technical summary for panels, then enumerate major flaws (requiring revision or rejection) and minor points (editorial/clarifying). Avoid vague statements; for each criticism, where possible, offer specific remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justified overall recommendation and alignment with scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: State a clear recommendation (e.g., accept/reject/fund/not fund/major revision/minor revision) and ensure it follows from evaluative comments and any numeric scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using numeric scales, provide how you applied the scale and why. Reconcile any apparent mismatch between high score and critical comments by explaining trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scores/criteria scales with explicit interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: When forms require numeric or categorical ratings, apply them consistently and explain borderline judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define what each score means in practice (e.g., 5 = outstanding, 1 = unacceptable). For multidisciplinary proposals, explain how you weighted different evaluation dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish confidential remarks to panel from comments for applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate comments intended only for the review panel/agency from those the applicant will see, using the provided confidential remarks field when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confidential notes sparingly and only for matters that cannot be made public (e.g., suspected misconduct, sensitive proprietary info). Ensure applicants receive sufficient feedback to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: professional, respectful and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain courteous, non-personal language; focus on the work, not the author, and frame criticisms as opportunities for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inflammatory adjectives and stay away from personal attacks. Provide examples of how to rephrase harsh criticisms into constructive suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance and mitigation of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of potential conscious or unconscious biases (gender, nationality, institution, language) and assess submissions on merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on whether peripheral factors are influencing judgement. If necessary, flag a potential bias and suggest blind review or additional reviewers from varied backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and traceability across reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your assessment is internally consistent and that key judgments are traceable to evidence in the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When changing initial impressions during review, document why. Where panels reconcile divergent reviews, indicate which evidence led to the final view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling suspected misconduct or plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suspect plagiarism, fabrication or other misconduct, report it through the confidential channel rather than raising it publicly in the review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific indicators (identical text passages, impossible data patterns) and supply references or examples to aid investigation; do not make unverified accusations in public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the reviewer in multidisciplinary assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing multidisciplinary work, limit judgements to your areas of expertise and clearly label cross-disciplinary uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which parts of the proposal you could evaluate confidently and which require input from other disciplines; recommend additional expert reviewers where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel and chair responsibilities in using reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels and chairs should use reviewer reports as input, reconcile divergent views transparently, and document reasons for final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairs must ensure fair discussion, avoid dominance by single reviewers, and record how major concerns were addressed in the decision. Use scores and qualitative comments jointly when justifying outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, calibration and quality control for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisers should provide guidance, calibration exercises or exemplars to align reviewers' standards and scoring practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend sample reviews, scoring anchors, and post-review audits to improve consistency. New reviewers should be mentored or paired with experienced reviewers where possible.
